kind: A screen by slope on the server's fan2 test bed, two seeds, 6,000 and 24,000 updates: a gated cell that multiplies two drives of either sign.
why: In floats the product of two signed drives (the bilinear control gate) does not fall behind the Transformer's gated unit as data grows (growth -0.027 on the mean of two seeds) and is the nearest of the control gates to it after 24,000 updates, 0.006 behind, where the ramp gate is 0.024 behind and the plain rectifying unit 0.015 and growing (bounded_gates_in_floats.json, plain_units_with_data.json). By that record's reading a cell may multiply two drives of either sign and needs no side on which its gate is shut. The homeostatic ramp gate (homeostatic_gates_with_data.json) showed that a spiking gate held in range catches up with data, but it carries the ramp's level cost. The signed gate built here (819b545, --granule-gate-signed) has no rest and fires on both rails, so the body fires the product of the gate's signed count and the value's signed charge; its synapses keep their first total strength, as the homeostatic gate's do, so the product stays in range. It adds one buffer a layer and no parameter, and keeps every count exact under any cut of the stream.
base: The runs of proportional_gates_with_data ending in -base (pg-6k-s1-base 1.61344, pg-6k-s2-base 1.61582, pg-24k-s1-base 1.47410, pg-24k-s2-base 1.48214), the same seeds and lengths; beside them home16 (hg-*) and pg16 (pg-*-gate).
runs: sg-6k-s1, sg-6k-s2, sg-24k-s1, sg-24k-s2: seeds 20001 and 20002, through sched/bin/bed.sh stack with --lr 1.2e-3 (and --steps 6000), on the code copy of 819b545 (v17x), on GPU 0 at priority 33.
measure: As homeostatic_gates_with_data: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes; each run paired with the base and with home16 of its seed and length; experiments/gap_by_piece.py (near 240, far 8,192); the pulses a byte; experiments/gate_state.py on the 24,000-update runs.
reading: The shared reading of experiments/read_lead_study.py against the base: a fix for late learning if at 24,000 updates its mean lead is at least 0.010 with both seeds ahead and it has grown by at least 0.005 since 6,000; a lead at 24,000 without that growth is a constant gain; anything else fails. A fix or a constant gain of at least 0.010 sends the signed gate to full size at full length (90,000 updates, a record of its own written before that run). If it fails but its lead grows by at least 0.005 from 6,000 to 24,000 updates, it gets the same pair at 96,000 updates as the homeostatic gate (homeostatic_gate_at_length.json), in a record written then. Beside the reading: whether the signed gate stands nearer the base than home16 at 24,000 updates.
seen_before_recording: bounded_gates_in_floats.json, plain_units_with_data.json, homeostatic_gates_with_data.json with their results; the laptop's check of an unsigned multiplying gate under the lifting pool without scaling (0.067 behind the lifted plain stack after 2,250 updates, design stage); the arm's recipe trained two updates on the server's CPU. No run of this arm has trained.

A third seed on the laptop's bed, which stood idle: sg-6k-s3 and sg-24k-s3, seed 20003, the laptop runner's recipe with --lr 1.2e-3 (and --steps 6000), --granule-gate 4 --granule-inner-gate --granule-gate-signed --granule-cells 681 --pool-lifts-ceiling, on a frozen copy of 819b545, paired with lift-6k-s3 (1.620623) and lift-24k-s3 (1.483491), the lifted plain bed of the laptop's shape. It is reported beside the server's two seeds and does not change the verdict.

result.verdict: Fails by the shared reading, and does not catch up: the signed gate is 0.0197 and 0.0154 behind the base after 6,000 updates and 0.0263 and 0.0185 behind after 24,000 (mean 0.0176 and 0.0224), so its distance grows with data (by 0.0048). No pair at 96,000 updates follows. After 24,000 updates it is 0.0203 and 0.0150 behind home16.
result.reading: The product of two signed drives, the gate nearest the Transformer's unit in floats, does not carry over to spikes in this form, and the census names why. A signed gate's open states let in 0.69 to 2.21 times the value by level, so its cells fire about 22,200 pulses a byte where home16's fire about 9,000; under the budget of 113,000 the reads are left with about 17,000 pulses a byte where home16's keep about 35,000. The cells' product takes the pulses that the reads need, and the loss falls on new contexts (0.023 to 0.028 behind the base after 24,000 updates). A gate that never lets in more than its value, as the homeostatic ramp does, keeps the reads' share. The cell that multiplies has to pay for its product inside the cell's own range, or it starves the rest of the stack; ramp gates held in range stay the candidate, and their pair at 96,000 updates (homeostatic_gate_at_length.json) decides whether they pass the plain cell.

result_laptop_seed.reading: As on the server's two seeds: the signed gate is behind the plain cell at both lengths and falls further behind with data (by 0.0075 from 6,000 to 24,000 updates, where the server's seeds fell by 0.0048). The third seed, on the laptop's shape of the bed, does not change the verdict (fail).
